mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined in each of the last four weeks (-13.6 to -20.0). This monotonic downward momentum reflects persistent behavioral caution that will continue to suppress retail visits over the next four weeks absent any reversing signal.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean over the last 28 days, breaking the observed four-week monotonic decline.

mechanism_narrative: An accelerating week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (from -11.9 to -17.9, with a -4.3 point jump in the latest week) signals tightening public-space restrictions. Once this acceleration crosses a threshold, retail outlets face similar restriction pressure, pulling RETAIL_REC further down over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -13.6 to -17.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks despite PARKS declining more than 4 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen each week (4.1 to 5.1) while GROCERY_PHARM has fallen sharply (17.6 to 10.7). The joint pattern of more time spent at home combined with reduced essential-errand trips indicates households are consolidating outings and reducing discretionary movement, which jointly depresses RETAIL_REC beyond what either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 4.1 to 5.1 while GROCERY_PHARM fell from 17.6 to 10.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks even as RESIDENTIAL continues rising and GROCERY_PHARM continues falling, indicating no joint suppressive effect.

mechanism_narrative: The co-decline of RETAIL_REC and PARKS alongside persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility is characteristic of a restriction-tightening regime in which non-essential and outdoor venues are curtailed together. Under this regime the mechanism predicts continued joint decline of RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC and PARKS both declined while RESIDENTIAL rose over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and PARKS decouple, with RETAIL_REC recovering while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, contradicting the joint-restriction pattern.

mechanism_narrative: Delhi's winter season brings deteriorating air quality and falling temperatures that reduce outdoor and leisure activity independent of policy. The parallel decline in PARKS and RETAIL_REC reflects this seasonal effect, which is expected to persist and deepen over the next four weeks as winter conditions continue.
evidence_refs: fact:both PARKS and RETAIL_REC show sustained declines over the snapshot window
failure_condition: PARKS and RETAIL_REC diverge in direction, or RETAIL_REC rebounds despite continued PARKS decline, indicating the seasonal mechanism is not operative.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has steadily recovered (-9.9 to -4.4) while TRANSIT has stayed roughly flat (2.7 to 2.6), implying commuters are returning to offices via private rather than public transport. This stabilizing commute pattern signals renewed economic activity that should spill over into higher retail footfall with a lag, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases for three consecutive weeks while TRANSIT changes by less than 1 point
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose each week from -9.9 to -4.4 while TRANSIT stayed near 2.6-3.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next four weeks despite WORKPLACES rising for three or more consecutive weeks with stable TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has fallen from 17.6 to 10.7, approaching baseline levels. This tapering suggests the recent elevated essential-shopping behavior (e.g., stockpiling) is receding, and in the short term reduced overall mobility momentum will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed for one more week before any broader recovery could emerge.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined from 17.6 to 10.7 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a GROCERY_PHARM reading below 10 points, contradicting the predicted short-term suppression.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has remained nearly flat (2.7 to 2.6) even as WORKPLACES improves and RETAIL_REC worsens, indicating a transitional regime where mobility signals are decoupled and not yet synchronized into a coherent recovery or decline. In this mixed regime, near-term RETAIL_REC is expected to keep falling for at least one more week before signals re-align.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT stayed flat near 2.6-3.1 while RETAIL_REC fell from -13.6 to -20.0
regime_hint: transitional regime with divergent mobility signals
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week while TRANSIT remains flat, indicating the decoupled-signal mechanism does not hold.
